reuse.why: Builds on the tree's existing single weekend rule (applyWeekendRule / applyWeekendRuleToDay / getDateWithSkippedWeekend) and skipsWeekendOccurrences, threading holidays through them instead of adding parallel logic.

duplication.why: The holiday/weekend test is defined once in isNonWorkingDay; the per-site daily-skip filter `!skipsWeekendDays || !isNonWorkingDay(...)` and the `7 + holidays.length` look-ahead heuristic remain repeated across getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange and schedule-template.

placement.why: isNonWorkingDay and the moving loop live in shared/schedules.ts next to the existing weekend rule; server sites only pass config.holidays.

scope.why: Only the holiday threading, the off-day predicate, the type field and parseRecurDate change; an unused date-fns import is removed as a direct consequence.

maintainability.why: The off-day definition is in one exported function, so extending it later is a one-place edit; the holidays parameter threaded through three helpers and the repeated filter are mild friction.

disguised_duplication.where: The repeated daily-skip filter is the pre-existing per-site structure with the predicate swapped for the shared isNonWorkingDay, not a reshaped copy of the rule.

one_place.where: isNonWorkingDay in packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts decides weekend-or-holiday for both moving (getDateWithSkippedWeekend via applyWeekendRule) and daily skipping in getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange and schedule-template.
